'''Jaylon La Rone Tyson''' (born December 2, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]], the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]] and the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]]. He was drafted with the 20th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].

==Early life and high school career==
Tyson was born on December 2, 2002, and grew up in [[Allen, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://calbears.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jaylon-tyson/22525|publisher=[[California Golden Bears]]|title=Jaylon Tyson}}</ref> He attended [[John Paul II High School (Plano, Texas)|John Paul II High School]] in Plano and helped the team win their first state championship in his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year, during which he averaged 23.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/news/longhorns-freshman-jaylon-tyson-commits-texas-tech|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Longhorns Freshman Jaylon Tyson Commits To Texas Tech|date=January 9, 2022|author=Galatzan, Matt}}</ref>

Tyson then helped them reach the state semifinals with a 26–2 record as a [[Senior (education)|senior]], being named the district [[most valuable player]] and a first-team all-state selection while averaging 22.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.1 steals per game.<ref name="auto1"/> Ranked the 34th-best recruit in the 2021 class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] after having flipped from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2021/04/14/following-beard-tech-jaylon-tyson-joins-texas/7227192002/|newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|title=Once signed with Texas Tech, F Jaylon Tyson changes course, signs with Texas|date=April 14, 2021|author=Davis, Brian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/cal/basketball/jaylon-tyson-transfers-to-cal|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Cal Basketball Adds Texas Tech Transfer Jaylon Tyson|date=May 8, 2023|author=Curtis, Jake}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first year at Texas in the 2021–22 season, Tyson appeared in eight games, averaging 6.9 minutes and 1.8 points per game.<ref name="auto">{{cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2021/12/27/texas-jaylon-tyson-followed-chris-beard-ut-now-hes-transferring/9026264002/|newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|title=Freshman Jaylon Tyson followed Beard to Texas, now he’s transferring after eight games|date=December 27, 2021|author=Davis, Brian}}</ref> He then entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref name="auto"/> Tyson ultimately committed to play for Texas Tech, whom he had previously committed to play for in high school before flipping to Texas.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/01/09/tyson-scored-11-points-season-opener-against-houston-baptist-but-his-minutes-were-erratic-getting-do/9153979002/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Former four-star prospect Jaylon Tyson decides to return to Texas Tech|author=Silva Jr., Carlos|date=January 9, 2022}}</ref>

Tyson started 31 games for Texas Tech in 2022–23, the third most on the team, and averaged 10.7 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/cal-s-jaylon-tyson-leaves-texas-tech-trauma-18481758.php|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|title=‘On top of the world’: Cal’s Jaylon Tyson leaves Texas Tech trauma behind|author=Kroichick, Ron|date=November 12, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He ranked eighth in the [[Big 12 Conference]] in rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4499732/2023/05/08/jaylon-tyson-transfer-cal/|website=[[The Athletic]]|url-access=registration|title=Former Texas Tech wing Jaylon Tyson transferring to Cal: What he brings to the Bears|date=May 8, 2023|via=The New York Times|last=Moore|first=CJ|first3=Tobias|last3=Bass|first2=Sam|last2=Vecenie|name-list-style=and}}</ref> He entered the transfer portal for a second time after the season, citing "racist" comments made by head coach [[Mark Adams (basketball, born May 1956)|Mark Adams]], who was later suspended and resigned. Adams did not deny that racially insensitive comments were made, but did say the comments were linked to a Bible verse.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2023/04/16/tech-sports-roundup-jaylon-tyson-plots-transfer-according-to-report/70118850007/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Tech's Tyson bound for transfer portal, according to report|date=April 16, 2023}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2023/10/27/jaylon-tysons-texas-tech-case-ncaa-crackdown-on-second-time-transfers|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 27, 2023|author=Sweeney, Kevin|title=Jaylon Tyson's Case Is the Latest in NCAA's Crackdown on Second-Time Transfers}}</ref> Tyson eventually committed to the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-tech-red-raiders/2023/05/08/former-texas-tech-forward-jaylon-tyson-to-transfer-to-cal-reports-say/|newspaper=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|title=Former Texas Tech, Texas forward Jaylon Tyson to transfer to Cal, reports say|date=May 8, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In October 2023, the [[NCAA]] initially denied Tyson's eligibility waiver for being a two-time transfer, despite Tyson alleging discrimination, which the NCAA rules mentioned as valid criteria for an eligibility waiver. He eventually was granted eligibility on November 9 and entered the team's starting lineup. <ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Faraudo|title=Cal Bears basketball gets huge boost after NCAA approves Texas Tech star’s eligibility waiver|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2023/11/09/cal-bears-basketball-gets-huge-boost-after-ncaa-approves-texas-tech-stars-eligibility-waiver/|newspaper=[[The Mercury News]]|url-access=subscription|date=November 9, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 26, 2024, Tyson was selected with the 20th overall pick by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Select Jaylon Tyson with 20th Overall Pick in 2024 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-jaylon-tyson-240627|website=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=July 13, 2025}}</ref> and on July 3, he officially signed with the Cavs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign 2024 Draft Pick Jaylon Tyson|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-jaylon-tyson-signing-240703|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=July 3, 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Cleveland Charge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Cleveland Charge Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Cleveland-Charge/34/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 27, 2024}}</ref> Tyson made 47 appearances (three starts) for Cleveland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 3.6 points, 2.0 rebounds and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaylon Tyson 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683747/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 13, 2025, Tyson recorded a season-high 31 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and three steals in the Cavaliers' loss to the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]], 126–118.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers vs Cleveland Cavaliers Apr 13, 2025 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/ind-vs-cle-0022401189|website=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2025|access-date=February 28, 2026}}</ref>

On October 29, 2025, Tyson scored a season-high 19 points, grabbed five rebounds, and had three steals as the Cavaliers lost 105–125 to the [[2025–26 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs Boston Celtics Oct 29, 2025 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/cle-vs-bos-0022500128 |access-date=November 15, 2025 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> On January 16, 2026, Tyson scored a career-high 39 points, including going 7-for-9 from behind the three-point line, as well as five rebounds and four assists during a 117–115 win over the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]]. The performance included a game-winning assist to [[Evan Mobley]] in the final seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers vs Philadelphia 76ers Jan 16, 2026 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/cle-vs-phi-0022500589 |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> Tyson made 66 appearances (including 42 starts) for the Cavaliers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 13.2 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jaylon Tyson 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683747/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Tyson’s older brother Berron played [[college football]] at [[South Alabama Jaguars football|South Alabama]], where he now serves as a strength and conditioning coach, while his younger brother [[Jordyn Tyson|Jordyn]] currently plays [[wide receiver]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article274807796.html|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star]]|title=Once committed to Duke, 5-star basketball forward now considering KU Jayhawks, others|author=Bedore, Gary|date=April 28, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jaylon Tyson {{!}} Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1642281/jaylon-tyson/bio |access-date=November 21, 2024 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> His father John Tyson played football at [[Florida A&M Rattlers football|Florida A&M]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stanley |first=Logan |title=Hines Ward on ASU WR Jordyn Tyson: 'We haven’t scratched the surface' |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2024/10/09/asu-football-receiver-jordyn-tyson-family-legacy-brother-nfl-nba/75299218007/ |access-date=November 21, 2024 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US|date=October 9, 2024}}</ref>
